title: `SUM` of doubles: plain sequential
description: `SUM(DOUBLE)` adds each value to the state in turn (`state.value += input`), and partial states merge by plain addition. The order of the values depends on the parallel plan.

Order class: (a) each state adds its values in turn, in the order they reach it; partial states combine by one addition each, in the order threads finish (ungrouped: each thread's state into the global one under a lock; grouped: per-thread hash tables, and abandoned or spilled partitions, merged partition by partition). With more than one thread, or a spilled hash table, the sum is a tree of unknown shape whose leaves are sequential runs. A constant vector (a constant argument, or a constant-compressed segment of a stored table) adds fl(k·x) for its k ≤ 2048 rows in one multiplication (`RepeatedStateValue::Multiply`). (b) With u = 2⁻⁵³ and γ_k = ku/(1 − ku): sequential |ŝ − s| ≤ γ_{n−1} Σ|x_i|, to first order (n − 1)u Σ|x_i| (Higham §4.2); any tree γ_h Σ|x_i|, h the most additions on one value's path to the root, at most n − 1 (§4.2); with P partials merged in a chain h ≤ m − 1 + P, m the largest partial's count. A constant run's product adds at most u·k|x| for its k values, so every path stays within γ_{n−1} Σ|x_i| and within #85's `sumTolScaled`. (c) The source below; duckdb-float-sum-order's round-4 thread runs (one result at 1 thread, several at 2 and 8); the constant-argument probe below (`sum(0.1)` over 10 rows is 1.0, the same values from a table 0.9999999999999999). (d) At one thread, with no constant vector and no spilled partial, SEQUENTIAL. Otherwise the tree shape of ANY (`FloatSums.split` over `seq` leaves), so `sum_order`'s `extra` entry (SEQUENTIAL, citing this fact) holds at threads = 1 only. A constant run's fl(k·x) is no sequential sum (1.0 against 0.9999999999999999 for ten 0.1); a search found it among the tree sums of k copies for each k ≤ 40 over 300 random x, but its membership in `FloatSums` is unproved: the Lean side needs that lemma, or a behaviour that allows a product step.
`SUM` and `AVG` of no rows, or of NULLs only, are NULL for DOUBLE, FLOAT and integer arguments (`sum-empty`): the clustered sum's state starts unset and finalizes to NULL.
The docs are silent on the algorithm and on the constant run's product: a docs gap. No upstream test pins the constant run's product or the dependence on thread order; it may change between versions.
reference: `AggFn.fsum` is `floatSumCR` (D25): the exact sum of the doubles, rounded once to nearest with ties to even; a NaN, or `+∞` with `-∞`, gives NaN, and one kind of infinity gives it. NULL without values. An engine's own order of additions is within the plan's bound (`sum_order`, `StdModel.epsilon_sum_cr`).

evidence.note: RepeatedStateValue: a constant run adds `input * static_cast<double>(count)` in one step
RegularAdd: `state.value += input`; AddConstant goes to AddRepeated
BaseSumOperation: Operation per value, ConstantOperation per constant run
UnaryScatter: a constant input over one state calls ConstantOperation with the vector's count
UnaryUpdate (ungrouped): a CONSTANT_VECTOR input calls ConstantOperation
a constant-compressed segment scans as a CONSTANT_VECTOR
ungrouped: each thread's state combined into the global one under a lock, as threads finish
grouped: per-thread hash tables; abandoned and uncombined partition data appended as threads finish
GroupedAggregateHashTable::Combine: partial states combined chunk by chunk (CombineStates)
NumericSumOperation (double `sum`): RegularAdd, clustered local state copied in and out
Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms (2nd ed., SIAM 2002), ch. 4 Summation: §4.2 recursive, pairwise and any-order bounds; §4.3 compensated summation

notes: Read at tag v2.0.0 (commit d54cbbe3). Higham's chapter is the docs reference for the bounds; only the formulas are used.
The tree-membership search is a scratch Python script over IEEE doubles, outside the repository.

evidence.sql: SET threads = 1; SELECT sum(0.1::DOUBLE)::VARCHAR, avg(0.1::DOUBLE)::VARCHAR, fsum(0.1::DOUBLE)::VARCHAR FROM range(10); CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT 0.1::DOUBLE v FROM range(10); SELECT sum(v)::VARCHAR, fsum(v)::VARCHAR FROM t; SELECT sum(v ORDER BY i)::VARCHAR FROM (SELECT 0.1::DOUBLE v, i FROM range(10) r(i))
evidence.observed: constant argument: sum 1.0, avg 0.1, fsum 1.0; table column: sum 0.9999999999999999, fsum 1.0; sum(v ORDER BY i) 0.9999999999999999. 0.1 * 10 is 1.0 in double, the ten additions in turn 0.9999999999999999

provenance.notes: DuckDB 2.0.0 (Python, macOS arm64), a scratch script at threads = 1.
